notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (User-agent: * with specific path disallows, no blanket Disallow: / and no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot naming) permitted tier (a)/(b). Tier (a) plain HTTP fetch of homepage + sitemap.xml + sitemap/category_l1/l2/l3.sitemap.xml (requests) got the full l1/l2/l3 category slug inventory but the product-listing pages are client-rendered (React SPA on a 'proddist' platform, no __NEXT_DATA__/embedded JSON), so quantities were not visible via tier (a) alone. Escalated to tier (b): launched headless Playwright (chromium), rendered representative listing pages, and captured the page's own XHR calls to the site's public search API (https://www.urbanladder.com/ext/search/application/api/v1.0/products?f=<facet-filter>&page_id=0&page_size=N). This is the same JSON the rendered page itself uses to build its DOM (not a third-party API), so it counts as tier (b) DOM/network-response reading, not an invented endpoint. TREE METHOD: built the tree from the union of the l1_category/l2_category facet families returned by that API (l1_category=storage-furniture -> l2_category={living-storage,dining-storage,bedroom-storage,kids-storage} -> category={leaf slugs}) plus l1=lighting--decor (which nests the 'Furnishing' nav tab's l2 groups: home-linen, carpets-rugs, bathroom-accessories, kitchen-dining-accessories, home-decor, wall-art-decor, lamps-lighting) plus l1=dining-room and l1=bedroom-mattresses for a few directly-tagged leaves (chair-pads; pillows1, mattress-protectors, kids-bedsheets). Confirmed the site's real working leaf-category URL scheme is /products/?category=<slug>&department=urban-ladder-furniture (NOT the /products/?l3_categories=<slug>&department=... URLs listed in sitemap/category_l3.sitemap.xml, which silently fall through to the site-wide total, e.g. l3_categories=chair-pads rendered '36098 Products' with unrelated sofa/lamp items instead of filtering - a confirmed instance of the 'bad slug silently serves the wrong number' trap; category_l3.sitemap.xml URLs were therefore discarded as unreliable and not used for any row). Verified the working ?category= URL against 4 spot-check renders (category=chair-pads -> '3 Products'/chip 'Chair Pads'; category=table-mat -> '29 Products' of table covers/placemats/runners; category=bookshelves -> '428 Products'; category=room-divider -> '174 Products') and every value matched the API facet count exactly, and item_total for each parent facet call equals the exact sum of its children's counts (e.g. storage-furniture item_total=2707 = sum of its 18 leaf categories). QTY METHOD: qty = the 'count' field on the matching value inside the 'category' (or l2_category) facet of the search API response for that parent scope - this is the site's own exact per-category product count, the same number the rendered page displays as '<qty> Products'. EXCLUDED: Wall Mirrors (126, sits inside the Home Linen l2 bucket but is a mirror/decor product, not textile); Dinnerware (414, Kitchen & Dining Accessories bucket - tableware, not textile/storage); Home Decor l2 (Showpieces/Artificial Plants/Planters/Vases/Table Photoframes/Artificial Flowers - decorative accessories, neither textile nor storage); Wall Art & Decor l2 (Wall Accent/Wall Clocks/Wall Art/Wall Photoframes - Wall Decor boundary, no distinct textile-wall-hanging subcategory exposed); all pure-furniture l1 departments (Sofas & Recliners, Living [Coffee/Side/Console Tables, Accent/Lounge Chairs, Ottomans, Benches, Bar Stools], Outdoor Furniture, Study, remaining Dining Room leaves [dining sets/chairs/tables/benches], remaining Bedroom & Mattresses leaves [beds, mattresses, bunk beds, cribs, kids study tables/chairs]) - all Furniture per the furniture boundary in both rule files. Institutional-business/B2B l1 branch and Deals/Services/Value-Added-Service branches skipped as non-category promo/B2B scope, not product taxonomy. STORAGE BOUNDARY JUDGEMENT CALL: Urban Ladder's own top nav has a dedicated 'Storage Furniture' department, structurally distinct and separate from its Living/Bedroom/Dining/Study furniture departments - i.e. the site itself explicitly buckets these 18 leaves as Storage rather than plain Furniture (storage.md Sec21/27: 'if explicitly placed inside a Storage/Organization category, prefer Storage'). All 18 leaves under that department were therefore included in storage_rows, with confidence graded per how clearly the item's own primary function is storage/organization: HIGH for Bookshelves, TV Units, Wall Shelves, Shoe Racks, Kitchen Cabinets & Racks, Crockery Units, Wardrobes, Chest of Drawers, Kids Bookshelves, Kids Wardrobes, Kids Chest of Drawers; MEDIUM for Bedside Tables, Dressing Tables & Mirrors, Bar Cabinets, Coat Rack, Kids Bedside Tables (storage is a secondary function alongside another primary use); LOW + MANUAL REVIEW flag for Prayer Units and Room Divider (devotional-furniture / room-partition primary purpose, storage secondary at best, placed in the review queue per storage.md Sec42 rather than silently guessed either way). Kitchen Linen (qty 1) is LOW confidence: the single item ranked under that category name is a 'Holiday Bunting' decoration, not a conventional kitchen textile, so it is flagged for manual review rather than dropped or upgraded.
